Elavon Payment Gateway API (2025-10-01)

Download OpenAPI specification:

Elavon Payment Gateway Helpdesk

Overview

This HTTP REST API is available for developers integrating with EPG for eCommerce.

The EPG API follows standard HTTP authentication and response codes and you can use it with most HTTP clients.

The EPG API tries to be precise with its responses but lenient with its requests. EPG defaults to case insensitivity where case is irrelevant and will use coercion to try resolving unexpected types.

The system only accepts JSON request bodies and returns UTF-8 encoded JSON response bodies pretty-printed for readability and with most fields included for discoverability.

The system supports HATEOAS and provides references between resources as hypermedia links. If needed, the system can accept resource IDs in requests instead.

We take security seriously. Communication with EPG must be over secure HTTP using at least TLS 1.2. EPG suppresses sensitive fields on responses.

PCI compliance is vital, and EPG provides options that allow integrators to reduce their own PCI scope.

Credentials

To get a user ID and password, integrators must send a primary email. Elavon sends an email that contains a link to the merchant UI as well as instructions on how to establish a password.

At the moment, Elavon onboards integrators into the EPG system manually, but the team is working on making this a more automated process in a future release.

Authentication

EPG's API authenticates using the HTTP BASIC method over secure HTTP using at least Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2.

Integrators receive a pair of API keys: one public and one secret. Elavon manages and provides API keys - future updates will add self-management as an option.

It's safe to include your public key in client-side code. Only hosted card resource operations authenticate using the public API key. Note that some fields will be suppressed when using a public API key. Check the hosted card resource for details. Their format, when used in actual scenarios, start with 'pk_'. Example:

pk_Yp6XYXCwkYjWFj9ByrhbDQD3

Never expose your secret key in client-side code. Only include your secret key in requests sent from a secure server. The API accepts the secret key for all requests. Their format, when used in actual scenarios, start with 'sk_'. Example:

sk_GWhvCdXCx6FWYhDqCRWVwtRk

Elavon provides integrators with a unique merchant alias for each merchant they're acting on behalf of.

Errors

Error responses generally have a standard JSON response. A failures array provides more information to help the integrator diagnose the issue.

4xx status codes show a problem with the request. Avoid retrying the request before addressing the problem. The following table shows some common failure codes and the causes that prompts them.

Failure Code Status Code Failure Description
badRequest 400 The request is invalid; correct all issues before resending.
unauthorized 401 A valid API key is required.
forbidden 403 Public API keys may only be used to create and retrieve hosted cards.
notFound 404 The requested resource does not exist.
methodNotAllowed 405 The given method may not be used here. Note that the X-HTTP-Method-Override header can only be used to override POST with either PATCH or DELETE
notAcceptable 406 The Accept request header must specify 'application/json;charset=UTF-8'; the Accept-Version request header if present, must reference a valid API version.
conflict 409 This request does not match the original, or the original request is still processing.
lengthRequired 411 Content-Length must be specified for this request.
payloadTooLarge 413 The request payload is too large.
unsupportedMediaType 415 The Content-Type request header must specify 'application/json'
tooManyRequests 429 Too many requests have been received too quickly for this API key.

5xx status codes show an unexpected server problem. EPG may be unable to return a standard error response for these.

Versioning

The current version is "1" and future versions will always be integral numbers. The client should specify which version they want using an "Accept-Version" request header. If not specified, EPG will assume the current version, but the response will include a "Warning" response header. The response will always include a "Version" header to show the version used. Example:

Accept-Version: 1

Elavon will avoid releasing versions with breaking changes. We will release some backwards compatible fixes without revising the version. If you are integrating with EPG, keep an eye out for some of the following changes:

  • New resources
  • New optional request query parameters and/or headers
  • New optional fields (Elavon may generate these randomly to ensure compliance)
  • Field order changes (while generally consistent, you should consider the order undefined)
  • New values for enumerated fields
  • New HTTP error codes
  • Changes to the format of IDs

Pagination

When listing resources, the API returns a standard PagedList. This resource includes links to the first and next pages in the list. If next page is null, then there are no more items. The default number of items for a page may vary by resource. To override the default, use the "limit" query parameter. By default, the limit is 10. The maximum limit for a pagination object is 200 entries. The "items" array contains the resources for the page.

See the example in Collection Filtering, where the filter "limit=2" indicates a limit of 2.

Collection Filtering

Certain resources have the option to apply filters. To specify a filter, provide one or more query parameters where the name starts with "filter" and the value is "fieldName_operator_value". Check the operations to see which fields support filtering and what operators each field supports. When using more than one filter, the resource must match every one of them.

Possible operators include:

  • eq (equals)
  • ne (not equals)
  • gt (greater than)
  • ge (greater than or equal)
  • lt (less than)
  • le (less than or equal)
  • like
  • in
  • contains
  • is
  • isnot

When filtering a field of type "URL resource", the value should be an ID (e.g. 6xxFwvM8BqmM6T6DcF3DyTB3).

When filtering a field of type "timestamp string", format the value as an RFC3339 Date/Time in the UTC time zone. The date/time separators, time section, seconds, milliseconds and Zulu time zone designator are all optional.

Example:

curl -X GET \
  "https://api.eu.convergepay.com/transactions?filter=type_eq_refund&filter=createdAt_gt_2020&limit=2" \
  -u 963myjmWbtt2DQgVpGyxcdW9:sk_GWhvCdXCx6FWYhDqCRWVwtRk \
  -H 'Accept-Version: 4' \

The previous example lists transactions via GET {endpoint}/transactions to retrieve all transactions created after the start of 2020.

The following sections support filters:

  • Retrieve Accounts
  • Retrieve Payment Links
  • Retrieve Payment Session
  • Retrieve Transactions
  • Retrieve Notifications
  • Retrieve Shoppers

Values

Resource ID

A unique string assigned as an identifier to individual resources. Each resource ID omits vowels to avoid confusing characters (O vs 0, for example). Treat Resource IDs as opaque strings with a 256 character limit when storing them.

Resource URL

A URL to an endpoint that will respond with the contents of an individual resource instance. Under each resource, a dropdown menu displays the available endpoints.

Timestamps

Timestamps use RFC3339 Date/Time format with the UTC time zone (e.g. "2018-02-01T05:10:20.152Z").

Currency

EPG represents currency amounts as strings using the natural or base units of the currency. A period is the decimal separator when the value needs one (e.g. 99,95€ would be "99.95").

Custom Reference / Custom Fields

Some resources accept integrator defined arbitrary custom fields. EPG does not use these fields for any operations. The API stores these fields with the associated resource and returns them when you request the resource.

Custom field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

As integrators have their own resources, these should be identified on the integrator side and only optionally provided to Elavon for cross-referencing purposes.

Operations

Each resource will have an ID that identifies it within a resource collection.

EPG uses commonly accepted HTTP methods to perform standard CRUD operations on resources (where allowed) using consistent resource paths.

Operation HTTP Request Successful Status Code
Create POST {resource-collection} 201 Created
Retrieve GET {resource-collection}/{id} 200 OK
Retrieve GET {resource-collection} 200 OK
Update POST {resource-collection}/{id} 200 OK
Delete DELETE {resource-collection}/{id} 204 No Content

Create operations will return the created resource.

HTTP Success vs. Transaction Success

Note that when creating and authorizing a transaction, EPG returns a 201 to show the transaction request processed, even if the transaction itself was declined. When creating transactions, use the state property of the Transaction to check whether EPG authorized or declined the transaction. If the transaction declined, the failures property provides an array of causes.

Deleting Resources

If the DELETE method is not allowed from the client, make a POST request instead with the optional request header "X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE".

The request for an update operation should only include those fields that have changed. To remove a field set its value to null.

CORS

Only hosted card operations support Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) requests from a browser. Initiate all other operations from a secure server.

Endpoint Health Check

To easily check if the API endpoint is live, simply send an unauthenticated GET request on the /health path. A 200 OK response with no content indicates a healthy API endpoint.

GET {{API Endpoint}}/health

Processor Accounts

Merchant profiles can have more than one processor account. At the moment, Elavon Payment Gateway currently supports one at a time. Each processor account tracks and processes transactions separately.

Multiple processor accounts are a good solution for merchants with the following use cases.

  • Merchants with multiple stores may have a processor account for each store.
  • Merchants tracking ecommerce separately from card-present purchases.

This resource is read only.

Orders

An order provides information on how much the shopper will have to pay at checkout. Orders also provide options to track:

  • What a shopper is paying for
  • What the shipping address is
  • The shopper's email address

Orders and Hosted Payments Pages

Initiating a Payment Session requires an order to inform how much the payment session should charge to the customer.

Hosted Payments Data Capture

Elavon Payment Gateway captures the shipTo and shopperEmail properties of a submitted Order. If the Hosted Payments Form is set to display Shipping Address fields to the customer, these fields will automatically populate with the values in the shipTo property.

Create Order

Creates an order.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json

object (Order)

required
object (PositiveAmountAndCurrency)

Total for all items

description
string <= 255 characters

Description, which appears on the dashboard and might appear on receipts

Array of objects (OrderItem) <= 64 items

Line items, 64 max

object (Contact)

Shipping contact details

shopperEmailAddress
string <= 254 characters

Shopper's email address

shopperReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the shopper, such as a purchase order

orderReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional order reference which we'll display in the merchant dashboard.

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

Responses

EPG SandBox

https://uat.api.converge.eu.elavonaws.com/orders

EPG Production

https://api.eu.convergepay.com/orders

Payment Links

A payment link is a link to a Checkout page that a merchant can send to a customer. A payment link has a set expiry timestamp - after this timestamp, the link becomes unusable.

A payment link cannot remain valid for longer than 1 year.

A canceled or expired payment link cannot be used to create a transaction.

Create PaymentLink

Create a Payment Link.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json
account
string <url> (ResourceURL<Account>)

Account Resource URL. Defaults to merchant.

returnUrl
string <url> <= 2048 characters https?://[^/]{2,}.*

URL to redirect a shopper to after collecting payment details.

expiresAt
required
string <date-time>

The expiration timestamp. A payment link must expire within 1 year of its creation.

doCancel
boolean

Cancel payment link. Defaults to false.

doCapture
boolean
Default: true

This value will be passed along to any transaction created later in the payment flow. See doCapture on transaction

description
string

Descriptive text indicating the purpose of the PaymentLink

required
object (AmountAndCurrency)

Total payment amount.

conversionLimit
integer

Number of times the PaymentLink may be used to complete a Transaction

object (DebtorAccount)

Account information required for MCC 6012/6050/6051 merchants

orderReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional order reference which we'll display in the merchant dashboard.

shopperEmailAddress
string <= 254 characters

Shopper's email address, useful for fraud detection and to provide a receipt

useStoredPaymentMethod
boolean

When 'true', a shopper must be provided. The HPP will force the use of a stored payment method: customer will either pick an existing one (if applicable) or the payment information they enter will get saved to the associated shopper.

When 'false', HPP will not present any existing stored payment methods to the customer and the customer will not be asked if they would like to save the payment method to their profile.

When 'null' or not provided, if a shopper is associated with the payment session, the user will have the option to select from any stored payment methods attached to their shopper record. They will also be able to enter new payment information and optionally save it to their profile.

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

shopper
string <url> (ResourceURL<Shopper>)

Shopper Resource URL

Responses

EPG SandBox

https://uat.api.converge.eu.elavonaws.com/payment-links

EPG Production

https://api.eu.convergepay.com/payment-links

Payment Link Events

A payment link event is automatically created by the system when certain actions occur concerning a payment link. Examples are transactions made from a payment link or email reminders sent to the customers.

A payment link event can only be created if the corresponding payment link is active and has not yet reached its conversion limit. In addition, only payment link events with the 'reminderSent' type can be manually created.

Create PaymentLinkEvent

Create a Payment Link Event.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json
paymentLink
required
string <url> (ResourceURL<PaymentLink>)

PaymentLink Resource URL

type
required
string (PaymentLinkEventType)
Enum: "payment" "reminderSent" "unknown"

Type of event. You can only create payment link events with the 'reminderSent' type.

createdBy
string <= 255 characters

Who or what created the transaction? When created in Elavon's virtual terminal, this will be the email address of the currently logged in user. When created otherwise, the integrator may optionally provide any value that helps answer this question.

shopperEmailAddress
required
string

Shopper's email address, required if event type is 'reminderSent'.

Payment Sessions

A payment session drives the way a transaction will process and sets the presentation for a customer's checkout.

Creating a Payment Session

To create a payment session, you will need to have an Order resource created ahead of time. This Order will inform the payment session on the amount to charge the customer and can pass information on the customer's shipping address to pre-populate fields in the hosted payment form.

Some of the data passed during creation are used to control the payment session behavior. Other fields are updated after the payment session has been created to collect various data needed to create the transaction while the HPP is being used by the customer.

The following fields can be potentially set after creating the payment session as the customer makes various selections:

  • expiresAt
  • paymentLink
  • forexAdvice
  • surchargeAdvice
  • transaction
  • hostedCard
  • storedCard
  • googlePayPayment
  • applePayPayment
  • pazePayment
  • blik
  • shopper
  • debtorAccount
  • threeDSecure
  • shopperEmailAddress
  • billTo
  • shipTo
  • shopperLanguageTag
  • doReset
  • createdBy

However, it is unlikely that these fields need to be set when creating the payment session.

Checkout Experience

The payment session sets which display mode a customer will view while checking out.

After creating a payment session, you will need to call the payment session using the lightbox script or redirect the customer to the URL of your hosted payments form. For more information on how to do this, refer to the Hosted Payments Redirect page.

Depending on the information passed when creating the payment session, the checkout page your customer sees will pre-fill billing and shipping address fields.

For more information on how the payment session displays to the customer, refer to the Hosted Payment Page Integration Guide.

Retrieve PaymentSession

Retrieve a payment session resource by ID.

Supported Filters:

  • paymentLink_eq_id
  • customReference_eq_string

string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

object (PaymentSession)

expiresAt
string <date-time>

Expiration timestamp

paymentLink
string <url> (ResourceURL<PaymentLink>)

PaymentLink Resource URL

forexAdvice
string <url> (ResourceURL<ForexAdvice>)

ForexAdvice Resource URL

surchargeAdvice
string <url> (ResourceURL<SurchargeAdvice>)

Surcharge Advice Resource URL

transaction
string <url> (ResourceURL<Transaction>)

Transaction Resource URL

hostedCard
string <url> (ResourceURL<HostedCard>)

HostedCard Resource URL

storedCard
string <url> (ResourceURL<StoredCard>)

StoredCard Resource URL

hostedAchPayment
string <url> (ResourceURL<HostedAchPayment>)

HostedAchPayment Resource URL

storedAchPayment
string <url> (ResourceURL<StoredAchPayment>)

StoredAchPayment Resource URL

googlePayPayment
string <url>

GooglePayPayment obtained through the create Google Pay payment API call. Required for 'ecommerce' 'sale' transactions.

applePayPayment
string <url>

ApplePayPayment obtained through the create Apple Pay payment API call. Required for 'ecommerce' 'sale' transactions.

pazePayment
string <url>

PazePayment obtained through the create Paze payment API call. Required for 'ecommerce' 'sale' transactions.

object (Blik)

BLIK object containing a six-digit code. This value is not returned.

shopper
string <url> (ResourceURL<Shopper>)

Shopper Resource URL

object (DebtorAccount)

Account information required for MCC 6012/6050/6051 merchants

object (ThreeDSecure)

Additional data that's only needed for 3-D Secure version 2 processing.

shopperEmailAddress
string <= 254 characters

Shopper's email address, useful for fraud detection and to provide a receipt

object (Contact)

Billing contact details that will be used by default for the hosted card

object (Contact)

Shipping contact details

shopperLanguageTag
string <= 255 characters

The IETF language tag optionally chosen by the shopper in the Hosted Payment Page, which may vary from the defaultLanguageTag.

shopperInteraction
string (ShopperInteraction)
Default: "ecommerce"
Enum: "ecommerce" "mailOrder" "telephoneOrder" "merchantInitiated" "inPerson"

The type of interaction with the shopper that generated this payment session.

  • ecommerce : The shopper generated this transaction with an ecommerce interaction.
  • mailOrder : The shopper generated this transaction with a mail order.
  • telephoneOrder : The shopper generated this transaction with a telephone Order.
  • merchantInitiated : A merchant generated this transaction without shopper involvement.
  • inPerson : The shopper generated the transaction in-person with a physical payment method (e.g. POS terminal).
doReset
boolean

Determines whether or not the HPP will be reset

createdBy
string <= 255 characters

Who or what created the payment session?

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

Create PaymentSession

Create a payment session.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json

object (PaymentSession)

expiresAt
string <date-time>

Expiration timestamp

account
string <url> (ResourceURL<Account>)

Account Resource URL. Defaults to merchant.

order
required
string <url> (ResourceURL<Order>)

Order Resource URL for which payment is being requested

allowedPaymentMethods
Array of strings (PaymentMethod)
Items Enum: "Card" "BLIK" "ACH"

Used to specify the payment methods allowed to be shown in the hosted payments page.

allowedPaymentMethodOrigins
Array of strings (PaymentMethodOrigin)
Items Enum: "Card" "Apple Pay" "Google Pay" "Paze" "BLIK" "Polish Bank Transfer" "ACH" "Unknown Wallet"

The allowed origins of the payment methods listed in the allowedPaymentMethods field.

paymentLink
string <url> (ResourceURL<PaymentLink>)

PaymentLink Resource URL

object (NonNegativeAmountAndCurrency)

Sales Tax

forexAdvice
string <url> (ResourceURL<ForexAdvice>)

ForexAdvice Resource URL

surchargeAdvice
string <url> (ResourceURL<SurchargeAdvice>)

Surcharge Advice Resource URL

transaction
string <url> (ResourceURL<Transaction>)

Transaction Resource URL

hostedCard
string <url> (ResourceURL<HostedCard>)

HostedCard Resource URL

storedCard
string <url> (ResourceURL<StoredCard>)

StoredCard Resource URL

hostedAchPayment
string <url> (ResourceURL<HostedAchPayment>)

HostedAchPayment Resource URL

storedAchPayment
string <url> (ResourceURL<StoredAchPayment>)

StoredAchPayment Resource URL

googlePayPayment
string <url>

GooglePayPayment obtained through the create Google Pay payment API call. Required for 'ecommerce' 'sale' transactions.

applePayPayment
string <url>

ApplePayPayment obtained through the create Apple Pay payment API call. Required for 'ecommerce' 'sale' transactions.

pazePayment
string <url>

PazePayment obtained through the create Paze payment API call. Required for 'ecommerce' 'sale' transactions.

object (Blik)

BLIK object containing a six-digit code. This value is not returned.

shopper
string <url> (ResourceURL<Shopper>)

Shopper Resource URL

object (DebtorAccount)

Account information required for MCC 6012/6050/6051 merchants

object (ThreeDSecure)

Additional data that's only needed for 3-D Secure version 2 processing.

shopperEmailAddress
string <= 254 characters

Shopper's email address, useful for fraud detection and to provide a receipt

object (Contact)

Billing contact details that will be used by default for the hosted card

object (Contact)

Shipping contact details

hppType
string (HppType)
Enum: "lightbox" "paymentLink" "fullPageRedirect" "hostedPaymentFields"

Hosted payments page type indicates the type of hosted payments page for the payment session, defaults to fullPageRedirect

returnUrl
string <url> <= 2048 characters https?://[^/]{2,}.*

URL to redirect to after payment details are collected. Required for hppType = fullPageRedirect. Must be null for lightbox and HPF.

cancelUrl
string <url> <= 2048 characters https?://[^/]{2,}.*

URL to redirect to if the shopper cancels. Required for hppType = fullPageRedirect. Must be null for lightbox and HPF.

originUrl
string <url> <= 2048 characters https?://[^/]{2,}.*

Origin where the hosted payment page will be embedded. Required if using the lightbox. Multiple origin URLs are allowed. Each URL must be separated by a space and each URL must follow the regex.

defaultLanguageTag
string <= 255 characters

Default IETF language tag, a tag that represents language names and countries, to be used in the Hosted Payment Page, such as en-GB meaning 'English (Great Britain)'.

shopperLanguageTag
string <= 255 characters

The IETF language tag optionally chosen by the shopper in the Hosted Payment Page, which may vary from the defaultLanguageTag.

shopperInteraction
string (ShopperInteraction)
Default: "ecommerce"
Enum: "ecommerce" "mailOrder" "telephoneOrder" "merchantInitiated" "inPerson"

The type of interaction with the shopper that generated this payment session.

  • ecommerce : The shopper generated this transaction with an ecommerce interaction.
  • mailOrder : The shopper generated this transaction with a mail order.
  • telephoneOrder : The shopper generated this transaction with a telephone Order.
  • merchantInitiated : A merchant generated this transaction without shopper involvement.
  • inPerson : The shopper generated the transaction in-person with a physical payment method (e.g. POS terminal).
doCreateTransaction
boolean
Default: false

Determines whether or not a Hosted Payment Page will perform an end to end transaction. If set to 'true', information a cardholder submits into a hosted payment form will automatically be used to create a Transaction resource. If set to 'false', the information submitted through the hosted payment form will automatically be used to generate a HostedCard resource. This value defaults to false. For more information on using the hosted payment form, see the integration guide.

In addition, if set to 'false', then digital wallets are not prompted in the hosted payments page (HPP).

doCapture
boolean
Default: true

This value will be passed along to any transaction created later in the payment flow. See doCapture on transaction

doThreeDSecure
boolean

Determines whether or not the HPP will perform 3-D secure validation

doReset
boolean

Determines whether or not the HPP will be reset

useStoredPaymentMethod
boolean

When 'true', a shopper must be provided. The HPP will force the use of a stored payment method: customer will either pick an existing one (if applicable) or the payment information they enter will get saved to the associated shopper.

When 'false', HPP will not present any existing stored payment methods to the customer and the customer will not be asked if they would like to save the payment method to their profile.

When 'null' or not provided, if a shopper is associated with the payment session, the user will have the option to select from any stored payment methods attached to their shopper record. They will also be able to enter new payment information and optionally save it to their profile.

createdBy
string <= 255 characters

Who or what created the payment session?

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

Payment Method Sessions

A payment session securely collects payment details from the shopper using our hosted payment page and sends them directly to our platform, allowing the merchant to minimize PCI DSS scope.

Create PaymentMethodSession

Create a payment method session.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json

object (PaymentMethodSession)

expiresAt
string <date-time>

An expiration timestamp.

account
string <url> (ResourceURL<Account>)

Account Resource URL. Defaults to merchant.

paymentMethodLink
string <url> (ResourceURL<PaymentMethodLink>)

Payment Method Link Resource URL.

shopper
string <url> (ResourceURL<Shopper>)

Shopper Resource URL

hppType
string (HppType)
Enum: "lightbox" "paymentLink" "fullPageRedirect" "hostedPaymentFields"

Indicates the type of hosted payments page for the payment session, defaults to fullPageRedirect.

returnUrl
string <url> <= 2048 characters https?://[^/]{2,}.*

URL to redirect to after payment details are collected

cancelUrl
string <url> <= 2048 characters https?://[^/]{2,}.*

URL to redirect to if shopper cancels

originUrl
string <url> <= 2048 characters https?://[^/]{2,}.*

Origin where the HPP will be embedded. Required if using the lightbox.

defaultLanguageTag
string <= 255 characters

Default IETF language tag, a tag that represents language names and countries, to be used in the Hosted Payment Page, such as en-GB meaning 'English (Great Britain)'.

shopperLanguageTag
string <= 255 characters

The IETF language tag optionally chosen by the shopper in the Hosted Payment Page, which may vary from the defaultLanguageTag.

doThreeDSecure
boolean

Determines whether or not the HPP will perform 3-D secure validation

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

Responses

EPG SandBox

https://uat.api.converge.eu.elavonaws.com/payment-method-sessions

EPG Production

https://api.eu.convergepay.com/payment-method-sessions

Total Adjustments

Make an adjustment to the total and/or tip of an existing transaction. The transaction resource must have isTotalAdjustable set to true.

Retrieve all adjustments

Create total adjustment

Adjust the transaction's total/tip amount.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json
required

object (Transaction)

transaction
required
string <url> (ResourceURL<Transaction>)

Transaction Resource URL, suppressed when a public API key is used

object (PositiveAmountAndCurrency)

The cumulative new total amount.

object (AmountAndCurrency)

The positive or negative adjustment to the prior authorized amount.

object (NonNegativeAmountAndCurrency)

The cumulative new sales tax.

object (AmountAndCurrency)

The positive or negative adjustment to the prior salesTax amount.

object (NonNegativeAmountAndCurrency)

Tip amount.

object (AmountAndCurrency)

The positive or negative adjustment to the prior tip amount.

doCapture
boolean

If false, authorize only; if true (default), authorize and capture funds for settlement.

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

Hosted Cards

Hosted cards are single-use cards. This captures all payment details so you can reference them in a transaction without having your server handle card details.

Each hosted card is valid for 30 minutes after creation.

You can use this resource to create a transaction using the Transactions endpoint.

Create HostedCard

Creates a HostedCard resource.

BasicAuth
header Parameters

Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Request Body schema: application/json
required

object (HostedCard)

required
object (Card)

Card Details

doVerify
boolean (doVerify)
Default: false

If true, verify Card.

string <= 255 characters

object

Hsm Cards

The HsmCard resource is used to hold terminal card data so the data is only needed to be decrypted once. The resource expires as soon as it is used in a transaction or in approximately 30 minutes. By using this resource, multiple calls can be made to the server during terminal operations without having to decrypt the data again.

Create HsmCard

Creates a HsmCard resource.

BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

integer <int32>
Example: 1

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

required

object (HsmCard)

object (Card)

Card Details

accountEntryMode
required

object (DeviceInteraction)

Information when using a hardware terminal.

string <= 255 characters

object

Forex Advices

A foreign exchange advice. Forex Advices track the exchange rate of the currency the card is transacting in against the home currency of the card. Forex advices are only available for merchant accounts with Dynamic Currency Conversion enabled.

At least one of the following is required to create a forex advice request: storedCard, hostedCard, cardNumber, or panToken.

Creating a sale with a forex advice

After creating a forex advice resource, you can use it to initiate a sale using the customer card issuer's currency. To do this, create a transaction with the Transactions endpoint and include the forex advice Resource URL in your request. There is no need to set the total amount of transaction if a forex advice resource URL is already included in the request.

Create ForexAdvice

Creates a ForexAdvice resource. Each ForexAdvice captures a foreign exchange currency conversion operation.

Transactions

Payment transactions.

  • Create a 'sale' transaction to take payment.
  • Create a 'void' transaction and reference a parent 'sale' transaction to reverse a transaction that hasn't yet settled.
  • If settled, a 'refund' transaction should be created instead. Check the 'isAuthorized' field to see whether or not the transaction was authorized, regardless of type. If not authorized, check the 'failures' array to determine why.

Sale

A sale transaction authorizes a transaction with a Shopper's card. An authorized transaction will settle as part of batch settlement.

Void

Only unsettled transactions are voidable. When you void a transaction, it will not be settled as part of batch settlement and will not be charged to the shoppers card.

Refund

After a transaction has settled, you must refund it to return the settled amount of money (or a portion of the amount) to the customer.

Create Transaction

Create a Transaction.

Credential on file type, used with cards in a wallet, if applicable.

  • recurring - a series of scheduled transactions with a variable amount (e.g. monthly payments to a utility company where the amount varies depending on usage)

Update Transaction

Overwrite an existing Transaction.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
path Parameters
id
required
string
Example: c2fkpt276g6rf6pwmfxmbyjf

Transaction Resource ID.

header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json

object (Transaction)

terminal
any (ResourceURL<Terminal>)

Terminal Resource URL

object (NonNegativeAmountAndCurrency)

Sales Tax

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

invoiceNumber
string <= 25 characters

Optional invoice number.

marketSegment
string (MarketSegment)
Enum: "retail" "restaurant"

Market segment for this transaction, to be sent on to processor

shippingDate
string <local-date>

Optional shipping date.

credentialOnFileData
string <= 29 characters

Value returned when creating an initial transaction for an integrator-managed card. This should be saved and set for succeeding transactions with the same integrator-managed card.

object (DeviceInteraction)

Information when using a hardware terminal.

object (PointOfInteraction)

Information about location of interaction.

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

isHeldForReview
boolean

If true, the transaction was authorized but has been held for review. While this is true, no further processing will occur for this transaction. All held transactions can be reviewed by the merchant in their dashboard. To approve with the API, update this field to false. To decline instead, create a 'void' transaction.

isTotalAdjustable
boolean

If true, the authorized total for the transaction can be adjusted.

doCapture
boolean

If false, authorize only; if true (default), authorize and capture funds for settlement

object (DoAutoCaptureAfter)
doSendReceipt
boolean

Send receipt to shopper's email address. Default value is based on the merchant's back office configuration.

object (Signature)

Point of Sale Signature

object (PartialAuthorization)

Partial Authorization Information

Responses

EPG SandBox

https://uat.api.converge.eu.elavonaws.com/transactions/{id}

EPG Production

https://api.eu.convergepay.com/transactions/{id}

Apple Pay Payments

The Apple Pay Payments resources capture all of the components necessary for processing a payment with the Apple Pay digital wallet. The payment token contains the encrypted payment data needed for transaction processing along with the elements needed for decryption. This cannot be used in conjunction with a Google Pay payment. It may also be used when creating a payment session. The only fields of the request to pass in the Card field is the Contact info, if available.

Create ApplePayPayment

Create an Apple Pay payment.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json

object (ApplePayPayment)

account
string <url> (ResourceURL<Account>)

Account Resource URL.

object (Card)

Only the Contact billTo info can be provided alongside the token. This is optional, but it does provide a more complete response with the decrypted Apple Pay payment info.

token
string

The Apple transaction id, encrypted payment data and data elements used for decryption.

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

Google Pay Payments

The Google Pay Payments resources capture all the card information that is encrypted within a transaction that uses Google Pay as a form of payment. This cannot be used in conjunction with an Apple Pay payment. It may also be used when creating a payment session. Pass in the encrypted Google Pay string in the token variable and get the decrypted value in the form of a card object. The only field to pass in the card field in the request is the Contact info.

Create GooglePayPayment

Create a Google Pay payment.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json

object (GooglePayPayment)

account
string <url> (ResourceURL<Account>)

Account Resource URL.

object (Card)

Only the Contact billTo info can be provided alongside the token. This is optional, but it does provide a more complete response with the decrypted Google Pay payment info.

token
string

The encrypted payment data that is to be decrypted to gather the card info within.

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

Responses

EPG SandBox

https://uat.api.converge.eu.elavonaws.com/google-pay-payments

EPG Production

https://api.eu.convergepay.com/google-pay-payments

This captures all the card information that is encrypted within a transaction that uses PAZE as a form of payment. This cannot be used in conjunction with an ApplePay payment or a GooglePay payment. It may also be used when creating a payment session. Pass in the encrypted PAZE string in the token variable and get the decrypted value in the form of a card object.

Create PazePayment

Create a Paze payment.

BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

object (PazePayment)

object (Card)

Only the Contact billTo info can be provided alongside the token. This is optional, but it does provide a more complete response with the decrypted Google Pay payment info.

payloadId
required
string <= 64 characters

An alphanumeric string returned from PAZE that refers to the current token and sessionId.

sessionId
required
string <= 255 characters

An alphanumeric string returned from PAZE that refers to the current token and payloadId.

token
string

The encrypted payment data in JWT format associated with the payload ID and session ID that is to be decrypted to gather the card info within

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

Surcharge Advices

A surcharge advice calculates the amount of surcharge and provides an adjusted transaction total for specific card numbers. This feature must be enabled for the merchant.

At least one of the following is required to create a surcharge advice request: storedCard, hostedCard, cardNumber, or panToken. If the card entered in the request cannot be surcharged, an error code is returned. You will not be able to collect surcharge using that card. You can either request a new surcharge advice with a new card, or proceed with that card and not collect surcharge with it.

Note that surcharge advice support is for NA merchants only.

Create SurchargeAdvice

Create a surcharge advice.

Refund Surcharge Advices

A refund surcharge advice calculates the amount of refundable surcharge and provides an adjusted refund transaction amount using the previous surcharge advice and the original parent transaction. This feature must be enabled for the merchant.

Note that refund surcharge advice support is for NA merchants only.

Manual Batches

Allows you to mark transactions for manual settlement.

You can specify a list of transactions IDs, or send an empty list to mark all eligible transactions.

A transaction is eligible for manual settlement batching when it meets ALL of the following criteria:

  • Transaction status: Marked for capture (doCapture = true)
  • Review status: Not held for review (isHeldForReview = false)
  • Batch assignment: Not currently assigned to any settlement batch (both manualSettlementBatchId and settlementBatchId must be null)
  • Ownership: Belongs to the specified merchant ID and account ID in the request
  • Transaction type: Matches the specified transaction type (typically SALE). REFUND and VOID are not supported.
  • Creation date: Transaction timestamp falls within the specified date range (typically the last 30 days)
  • Authorization validity: Has a non-null expiration timestamp that's after the end date of the query range
  • Payment method: Not processed using excluded payment methods (BLIK, POLISH_BANK_TRANSFER, or ACH)

Shoppers

A Shopper resource is a collection of stored information about a shopper. After making a Shopper, Elavon Payment Gateway can display this information in the Elavon Payment Gateway UI and use it for the following use cases:

  • Saving frequently used shopper data.
  • Pre-populating fields in the checkout form for a Payment Session.
  • Providing information for a Transaction.
  • Saving payment information for the shopper as a Stored Card resource.
  • Applying subscriptions to shoppers with a Stored Card.

Subscriptions

A Subscription applies a Plan to the Stored Card of a Shopper. This association applies the instructions for a multi-payment transaction detailed in a Plan.

Create Subscription

Create a subscription for a customer. The subscription will generate recurring payments based on timing and amount details from a plan and using a specific stored card for the payment.

Authorizations:
BasicAuth
header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media types the client will accept.

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json
required

object (Subscription)

plan
required
string <url> (ResourceURL<Plan>)

Plan Resource URL.

Plan determines the billing details and their frequency.

account
string <url> (ResourceURL<Account>)

Account Resource URL. Defaults to merchant.

doSendReceipt
string
Default: "DEFAULT"
Enum: true false "DEFAULT"

Send receipt to shopper's email address. The default value is 'DEFAULT', which will use the merchant setting for sending receipts for recurring sales

storedCard
required
string <url> (ResourceURL<StoredCard>)

StoredCard Resource URL

StoredCard to which all payments will be billed and which must belong to the provided Shopper.

storedAchPayment
string <url> (ResourceURL<StoredAchPayment>)

An ACH payment that is stored for a shopper and may be used for recurring payments.

surchargeAdvice
string <url> (ResourceURL<SurchargeAdvice>)

SurchargeAdvice obtained through the create surchargeAdvice API call.

initialSurchargeAdvice
string <url> (ResourceURL<SurchargeAdvice>)

SurchargeAdvice obtained through the create surchargeAdvice API call for initial bills.

billCount
integer <int32> >= 1

The total number of bills. May only be provided if not defined in plan.

timeZoneId
required
string

The time zone ID for date fields in the subscription. This follows the IANA Timezone Database Name convention.

firstBillAt
required
string <date>

The first bill date. This value anchors the billing interval and determines all future bill dates. For monthly and yearly billing intervals, if the first bill date occurs on the last day of the month then all future bill dates will be adjusted to occur on the last day of the month.

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

Responses

EPG SandBox

https://uat.api.converge.eu.elavonaws.com/subscriptions

EPG Production

https://api.eu.convergepay.com/subscriptions

BasicAuth
path Parameters
id
required
string

Subscription Resource ID

header Parameters
Accept
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Accept-Version
integer <int32>
Example: 1

API version requested by client.

Content-Type
string
Example: application/json;charset=UTF-8

Media type of the request body.

Request Body schema: application/json

object (Subscription)

doSendReceipt
string
Default: "DEFAULT"
Enum: true false "DEFAULT"

Send receipt to shopper's email address. The default value is 'DEFAULT', which will use the merchant setting for sending receipts for recurring sales

storedAchPayment
string <url> (ResourceURL<StoredAchPayment>)

An ACH payment that is stored for a shopper and may be used for recurring payments.

surchargeAdvice
string <url> (ResourceURL<SurchargeAdvice>)

SurchargeAdvice obtained through the create surchargeAdvice API call.

initialSurchargeAdvice
string <url> (ResourceURL<SurchargeAdvice>)

SurchargeAdvice obtained through the create surchargeAdvice API call for initial bills.

object (SubscriptionSurcharge)

Surcharge information if surchargeAdvice was created for the subscription

cancelAfterBillNumber
integer <int32>

The bill number after which no further billings will occur

customReference
string <= 255 characters

Optional reference provided by the merchant

object

Custom fields, an object containing arbitrary string values. Field names and values must not exceed 64 and 1024 characters, respectively.

EPG SandBox

Pan Tokens

Convert one or more PANs into PanTokens

  • You can exchange a Personal Account Number (card number) for a PanToken which is a tokenized version of the data that can safely be stored
  • This allows your integration to stay PCI compliant
  • A PanToken is unique to an individual merchantId and PAN combination

Create PanTokens
